definition: arXiv API topic queries of the first discovery rounds
terms_or_pattern: oversight; formal agent safety; agent security; agent alignment; multi-agent safety; corrigibility and power seeking; deception and control; memory and skills; evolving agents; safe decision making

name: Venue catalogues
definition: official proceedings screened in full: NeurIPS, ICML and ICLR downloads, PMLR, ACL Anthology, USENIX Security; publication status checked on dblp, Crossref and OpenAlex

name: Citation follow-up
definition: reference lists of five journal articles and one USENIX Security 2026 systematization paper

name: Curated lists
definition: three agent-security reading lists on GitHub and the arXiv identifiers listed in 176 GitHub awesome lists on AI and agent safety and security

name: Updates
definition: incremental arXiv harvests with the same rules until 15 October 2026; field statistics stop at 30 September 2026

name: In scope: digital agents
definition: safety, security, oversight or alignment of tool and API agents, coding agents, browser and GUI agents, assistants, agentic workflows and multi-agent systems

name: In scope: embodied agents
definition: safety of embodied or physical-world agents whose decisions come from a foundation model (LLM, VLM or VLA robots, driving and drones)

name: In scope: foundational safety
definition: oversight and control (corrigibility, deception, scheming, sabotage, monitoring); the instruction-data trust boundary; evaluations of dangerous capabilities that matter for autonomous action; surveys and agendas on the safety of agents or autonomous AI

name: Out of scope
definition: general capability or task performance; flaws of a base model alone with no agent (for example chat-model jailbreaks or backdoors); using an agent as a security tool; alignment mechanisms such as reward modelling and preference learning; reinforcement-learning or physical systems without a foundation model; non-scholarly items

name: Decision rules
definition: R1 object and safety contribution both named; R2 a safety tool is not safety of the tool; R3 explicit foundational safety retained; R4 a consequential domain is not a safety contribution; R5 embodied agents with a learned policy or foundation model; R6 boundary = one question answered from the full text; R7 safety verification before deployment counts, reliability failures need an explicit safety link, a mixed survey counts through a substantive safety section

name: Screening process
definition: first pass on title and abstract; a second model reviews every first-pass inclusion and boundary case; boundary cases resolved from full-text excerpts; remaining cases reviewed by the project owner; every decision keeps its reason and a verbatim quote
